{"rules": ["Model consistently underestimates price spikes when recent history shows a sharp upward trend (e.g., Example 1 & 2 where price jumped from ~73 to ~84); apply +5% to forecast target if last 3 days show >5% daily gain.", "Model exhibits severe mean reversion bias in bearish regimes; when sentiment is low (0.00) and history shows declining prices (e.g., Example 5), model fails to capture volatility, resulting in a flat trajectory while true outcome swings wildly; increase forecast variance by 15-20% during low-sentiment periods.", "Model ignores immediate momentum shifts; if sentiment rises slightly (e.g., 0.20-0.33) amidst rising prices, the model's flat or slow-rising forecast lags significantly behind true outcomes; add a momentum correction factor equal to the average daily gain of the last 5 days.", "In Example 4, despite high sentiment (0.50), the model failed to anticipate a sustained rally above 81; rule: when sentiment >0.30 and price is near support levels, increase forecast floor by 2% to account for breakout probability.", "Model tends to smooth out volatility in the first 7 days of the 30d horizon; true outcomes often show higher dispersion (spikes up/down) than predicted; apply a volatility multiplier of 1.15 to the standard deviation of the last 18 days when projecting the first week."]
